en.text: Source / locator: Ibn Kathir, Tafsir (Abridged), Qur’an 24:27–29; section “Seeking Permission and the Etiquette of entering Houses”.

Scholarly position / paraphrased argument: The commentary connects greeting and permission with the comfort of occupants, explains that a visitor must leave after three unanswered requests, and treats an instruction to return as something to accept rather than resent.

Verification / translation sources: Ibn Kathir (Abridged), English text on Quran.com, inspected at the verse-group and named passage. Compiler’s English–Urdu paraphrase; not a claim to have collated the complete Arabic edition.
Relevance: Adds a practical account of boundaries and privacy to the Qur’anic permission clause.

Context / qualification: The three-request rule is conveyed through the commentary’s cited Prophetic evidence; it is not presented as words appearing in 24:27 itself. The embedded reports are not separately counted here.
Best use: Critical analysis / conceptual framework
Verify:
Source 1

تصدیق / تراجم کے ماخذ: قرآن ڈاٹ کام پر ابن کثیر کے مختصر انگریزی متن میں متعلقہ آیات اور عبارت دیکھی گئی۔ مرتب کا انگریزی و اردو مفہومی خلاصہ ہے؛ مکمل عربی ایڈیشن کے تقابل کا دعویٰ نہیں۔
مطابقت: قرآنی حکمِ اجازت کے ساتھ حدود اور خانگی حرمت کی عملی توضیح فراہم کرتا ہے۔
